scope: phase_C_cancel_parent_resolution; supplied full current source/tests and explicitly labeled integration diff if present

findings.title: Cancel acknowledgement omits external-call warning for jobs claimed after pre-read
findings.issue: control() reads state before queue.cancel() and derives the warning text from that pre-read state (line 167), but the warning callback fires only when the post-cancel attempts>0. In the real race where the pre-read saw queued/retry_wait but a worker claimed (attempts incremented) before cancel, the job may have an in-flight external call, yet the text omits 'Уже начатый внешний вызов мог продолжиться.' The test test_cancel_warning_uses_actual_attempts_if_worker_claims_after_status_read only covers the case where claims happen during the status read; the transition claim→cancel is not covered for the warning string.
findings.fix: Decide the warning text and callback from the authoritative post-cancel attempts/status (or the cancel return value plus a fresh read), not the pre-read state; include the warning whenever the job was ever leased/running (attempts>0 at cancellation). Extend the deterministic test to cover a claim that occurs strictly between the pre-read and the cancel UPDATE.

findings.title: Unknown aggregate with zero children is permanently unreconcilable and unrecoverable
findings.issue: The parent row is inserted as 'unknown' before any part attempt; a crash after the insert and before the first child leaves zero children. reconcile then returns the parent at delivery.py:297 without ever producing evidence, and deliver_result early-returns the existing aggregate (113-116), so no future explicit intent can deliver the message and no adapter can observe the unattempted state. This is consistent with the documented no-blind-retry/prepared boundary (unknown ≠ known failure) and test_aggregate_preparation_without_parts_never_authorizes_second_dispatch verifies it, so it is a deliberate availability loss, not permission escalation — but the operator has no documented reconciliation/new-intent path for this state.
findings.fix: Keep the non-replayable fence; surface the state explicitly in describe() (e.g. 'prepared before any part; requires explicit new owner intent or provider evidence') and document a bounded operator recovery path that requires new explicit owner confirmation rather than fabricating a known-failure or resuming automatically.

not_verified: src/prm/watch_jobs.py, src/prm/runtime/scheduler.py, src/prm/storage/actions.py, deletion.py, capabilities.py and bot/prm_handlers.py are not in the packet; only their inline usage in the supplied sources was reviewed.
Actual execution against a live/synthetic PostgreSQL instance was not performed; findings are static analysis of the supplied sources and tests.
Runtime composition/config validation in runtime_from_config and OperationsRuntime status semantics were not supplied.

Whether effect_lease is passed on all production deliver_result call sites outside the packet was not verified (ingress /result passes none; the delivery.py:93-96 guard covers the scheduled-effect case).
findings.summary: No P0: the supplied sources preserve fail-closed semantics — unknown/lost-ACK attempts are never resent (delivery.py:113-116, 204-208), unknown effect jobs are not reclaimed (jobs.py recover_expired→awaiting_reconciliation), reconciliation requires exact per-attempt and per-part evidence (delivery.py:290-307, 325-330) and a missing part cannot be inferred from another's receipt (test_multipart_missing_part_cannot_be_reconciled_by_one_aggregate_receipt), media MIME is allowlisted (ingress.py:75), and grants/reservations bind provider, purpose and data class per operation. Resolving the two #39 P1 claims: the aggregate-prepared-with-no-children case is not a correctness or safety defect — existing aggregate rows provably prevent any second dispatch (test_aggregate_preparation_without_parts_never_authorizes_second_dispatch and test_fake_server...confirm one send), and the recommended 'resume loop' would remove a durable, possibly billable fence contrary to the documented prepared/unknown no-blind-retry boundary; it is recorded below as a P2 availability/explicit-recovery gap only. The cancel race is real and remains partially unfixed: ingress.py:163-167 still derives the 'already started external call' warning from the pre-read state, so a job claimed between the pre-read and the cancel UPDATE can be cancelled with an in-flight call without the warning (callback firing is now correct via post-cancel attempts, but the user-facing text is not), which is a P1 information/acknowledgment defect. With one P1 present, verdict is FIX_P1_FIRST.
